$schema_note: M5 end-of-module quiz, three scenario items; correct_index is 0-based. The learner-facing stems and rationales are set in module.js (QUIZ_COPY).

items.stem: Emma, who runs operations at a manufacturer with 78 people, says: 'Finance tags 400-plus supplier card transactions a month by hand, because Xero can't read our job numbers.' Which prop do you lead with?
options: Prop 2, team cards with per-card limits
Prop 4, receipt capture with accounting sync
items.rationale: Emma's finance team tags receipts by hand for hours every month. Receipt capture with Xero sync removes that work, which makes Prop 4 the one to lead with.

items.stem: Tom, the founder of a Series-B SaaS company, says: 'We're hiring six engineers this quarter, and per-employee cards take forever.' Which reply uses his words instead of jargon?
options: Our spend-control platform orchestrates per-employee card issuance with best-in-class speed.
Our solution provides synergistic real-time visibility across your spend management surface.
We give you a 2-minute API call per new hire — you don't ping finance, you trigger the card from your HR tool.
We've got a leading expense-management orchestration layer that sits on top of your stack.
items.rationale: The API reply talks about Tom's new hires and gives him one number, two minutes per card. The other three are vendor jargon he would have to translate.

items.stem: You are 90 seconds into a call with Tom when S.K., his finance lead, joins. Tom hasn't mentioned FX, and you were about to pitch Prop 2. What do you do?
options: Ask S.K. a fresh diagnostic about her FX exposure before picking which prop to lead with for her.
Recap to S.K. what you and Tom agreed, then pitch Prop 2 in the same breath so the call keeps momentum.
Ignore S.K. and finish the Tom thread — you can email her separately after.
Acknowledge S.K. and pivot the whole call to Prop 2 (multi-user cards) since cards are universal.
items.rationale: S.K. owns the FX numbers, so ask her before you choose a prop. On L.D.'s call it was her answer that brought out the €1,900 a month.
